messages.content: You are a helpful assistant that can interact with a computer.

Please solve this issue: Writebook lets an editor drop images straight into a page's markdown body:
each image is uploaded once and then referenced inline from the page's
content. Delete that page, and the image never actually leaves the app — the
file survives on disk, and the record that tracks it survives in the
database, forever, even once any background work the deletion sets off has
finished running. We cleared out a batch of stale pages and the storage bill
barely moved.

Fix it so that after a page whose markdown has an embedded image is destroyed,
and once any background work that destruction triggers has run to completion,
neither the image's file nor the record tracking it exists anywhere in the app.

Uploading a new image into a page's markdown, and then fetching that image back
from the URL the app hands you for it, has to keep working exactly as it does
today.

module Leaf::Editable
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

  MINIMUM_TIME_BETWEEN_VERSIONS = 10.minutes

  included do
    has_many :edits, dependent: :delete_all

    after_update :record_moved_to_trash, if: :was_trashed?
  end

  def edit(leafable_params: {}, leaf_params: {})
    if record_new_edit?(leafable_params)
      update_and_record_edit leaf_params, leafable_params
    else
      update_without_recording_edit leaf_params, leafable_params
    end
  end

  private
    def record_new_edit?(leafable_params)
      will_change_leafable?(leafable_params) && last_edit_old?
    end

    def last_edit_old?
      edits.empty? || edits.last.created_at.before?(MINIMUM_TIME_BETWEEN_VERSIONS.ago)
    end

    def will_change_leafable?(leafable_params)
      leafable_params.select do |key, value|
        leafable.attributes[key.to_s] != value
      end.present?
    end

    def update_without_recording_edit(leaf_params, leafable_params)
      transaction do
        leafable.update!(leafable_params)

        edits.last&.touch
        update! leaf_params
      end
    end

    def update_and_record_edit(leaf_params, leafable_params)
      transaction do
        new_leafable = dup_leafable_with_attachments leafable
        new_leafable.update!(leafable_params)

        edits.revision.create!(leafable: leafable)
        update! leaf_params.merge(leafable: new_leafable)
      end
    end

    def dup_leafable_with_attachments(leafable)
      leafable.dup.tap do |new|
        leafable.attachment_reflections.each do |name, _|
          new.send(name).attach(leafable.send(name).blob)
        end
      end
    end

    def record_moved_to_trash
      edits.trash.create!(leafable: leafable)
    end

    def was_trashed?
      trashed? && previous_changes.include?(:status)
    end
end

# frozen_string_literal: true

require "active_support/core_ext/module/delegation"

# = Active Storage \Attachment
#
# Attachments associate records with blobs. Usually that's a one record-many blobs relationship,
# but it is possible to associate many different records with the same blob. A foreign-key constraint
# on the attachments table prevents blobs from being purged if they’re still attached to any records.
#
# Attachments also have access to all methods from ActiveStorage::Blob.
#
# If you wish to preload attachments or blobs, you can use these scopes:
#
#   # preloads attachments, their corresponding blobs, and variant records (if using `ActiveStorage.track_variants`)
#   User.all.with_attached_avatars
#
#   # preloads blobs and variant records (if using `ActiveStorage.track_variants`)
#   User.first.avatars.with_all_variant_records
class ActiveStorage::Attachment < ActiveStorage::Record
  define_model_callbacks :upload

  after_upload :mirror_blob_later
  after_upload :analyze_blob_later
  after_upload :create_variants

  # Set to true when immediate variants have been processed from local io,
  # so create_variants knows to skip them.
  attr_accessor :immediate_variants_processed

  # Set to true for fresh uploads (io provided), false for existing blobs.
  # Used to determine whether to run :upload callbacks in after_create_commit.
  attr_accessor :pending_upload

  ##
  # :method:
  #
  # Returns the associated record.
  belongs_to :record, polymorphic: true, touch: ActiveStorage.touch_attachment_records

  ##
  # :method:
  #
  # Returns the associated ActiveStorage::Blob.
  belongs_to :blob, class_name: "ActiveStorage::Blob", autosave: true, inverse_of: :attachments

  delegate_missing_to :blob
  delegate :signed_id, to: :blob

  after_create_commit :run_upload_callbacks, unless: :pending_upload
  after_destroy_commit :purge_dependent_blob_later

  ##
  # :singleton-method:
  #
  # Eager load all variant records on an attachment at once.
  #
  #   User.first.avatars.with_all_variant_records
  scope :with_all_variant_records, -> { includes(blob: {
    variant_records: { image_attachment: :blob },
    preview_image_attachment: { blob: { variant_records: { image_attachment: :blob } } }
  }) }

  # Called by Attached::Changes::CreateOne to handle the upload workflow for
  # fresh uploads. Processes immediate variants and analyzes from the local io
  # (avoiding a download round-trip), uploads the blob, then runs the :upload
  # callbacks.
  #
  # For existing blob attachments, the :upload callbacks are run via
  # after_create_commit instead.
  def uploaded(io:)
    blob.local_io = io

    process_immediate_variants_from_io(io)
    analyze_blob_from_io(io)

    io.rewind if io.respond_to?(:rewind)
    blob.upload_without_unfurling(io)

    # Persist analysis metadata if the blob was already saved (happens when
    # upload runs in after_commit, after the blob was saved via autosave).
    blob.save! if blob.persisted? && blob.metadata_changed?

    run_upload_callbacks
  ensure
    blob.local_io = nil
  end

  # Synchronously deletes the attachment and {purges the blob}[rdoc-ref:ActiveStorage::Blob#purge].
  def purge
    transaction do
      delete
      record.touch if record&.persisted?
    end
    blob&.purge
  end

  # Deletes the attachment and {enqueues a background job}[rdoc-ref:ActiveStorage::Blob#purge_later] to purge the blob.
  def purge_later
    transaction do
      delete
      record.touch if record&.persisted?
    end
    blob&.purge_later
  end

  # Returns an ActiveStorage::Variant or ActiveStorage::VariantWithRecord
  # instance for the attachment with the set of +transformations+ provided.
  # Example:
  #
  #   avatar.variant(resize_to_limit: [100, 100]).processed.url
  #
  # or if you are using pre-defined variants:
  #
  #   avatar.variant(:thumb).processed.url
  #
  # See ActiveStorage::Blob::Representable#variant for more information.
  #
  # Raises an +ArgumentError+ if +transformations+ is a +Symbol+ which is an
  # unknown pre-defined variant of the attachment.
  def variant(transformations)
    transformations = transformations_by_name(transformations)
    blob.variant(transformations)
  end

  # Returns an ActiveStorage::Preview instance for the attachment with the set
  # of +transformations+ provided.
  # Example:
  #
  #   video.preview(resize_to_limit: [100, 100]).processed.url
  #
  # or if you are using pre-defined variants:
  #
  #   video.preview(:thumb).processed.url
  #
  # See ActiveStorage::Blob::Representable#preview for more information.
  #
  # Raises an +ArgumentError+ if +transformations+ is a +Symbol+ which is an
  # unknown pre-defined variant of the attachment.
  def preview(transformations)
    transformations = transformations_by_name(transformations)
    blob.preview(transformations)

**Okay, deep breath. We have a situation. A *big* situation.** I've stumbled upon what looks like *two* critical bugs in `lib/rails_ext/action_text_markdown.rb`, and possibly more lurking elsewhere! This needs to be documented, and we are going to dive in!

**First, let's nail down what's happening in `lib/rails_ext/action_text_markdown.rb`.** The code includes an `ActiveSupport.on_load :active_storage_attachment` block, intending to include `ActionText::Markdown::Uploads`. However, this is wrong. Why are we waiting for a *specific* load hook when `ActiveStorage::Attached::Model` is already included in `ActiveRecord::Base` via the `ActiveStorage` railtie? This means that `has_many_attached :uploads` should be defined on the class immediately. This timing discrepancy is a major problem.

**This incorrect inclusion strategy creates two distinct issues.** First, if a request to upload an image is the *first* request on a Rails server, `ActiveStorage::Attachment` might not have been autoloaded yet. Consequently, calling something like `Page.first.body.uploads` or triggering `@markdown.uploads.attach` in `UploadsController#create` will result in a `NoMethodError`. This is a *major* potential pitfall, especially in development environments where eager loading is disabled. This is easily reproducible using a Rails runner *before* any fixtures that reference `ActiveStorage::Attachment` are loaded. And, if a background job or rake task or console runs `Page.find(id).destroy` without `ActiveStorage::Attachment` loaded first, `ActionText::Markdown` doesn't even have `has_many :uploads_attachments, dependent: :destroy`, so `ActiveRecord::InvalidForeignKey` or orphaned `active_storage_attachments`!

**The second bug is within `has_many_attached :uploads, dependent: :destroy`.** Even when `ActiveStorage::Attachment` *is* loaded, the `dependent: :destroy` option on `has_many_attached` is flawed. Let's trace this during a `page.destroy` operation. When destroying a page with an embedded image, it correctly destroys the `ActionText::Markdown` record and the associated `ActiveStorage::Attachment` record. *However*, the `dependent: :destroy` option on `has_many_attached` triggers a *direct* deletion of the attachments. The `after_destroy_commit :purge_dependent_blob_later` callback of `ActiveStorage::Attachment` is *not* triggered. This means that *neither* an `ActiveStorage::PurgeJob` is enqueued, *nor* is the `blob&.purge_later` called, so *both* the `ActiveStorage::Blob` record *and* the file on disk survive indefinitely! This is *exactly* what the prompt is describing!

**Wait, let's step back and consider the scope of this problem.** We have to expand our investigation beyond `page.destroy`. The prompt asks us to ensure that *after* a page is deleted, and any background jobs are completed, *neither* the image file nor the tracking record exists anywhere.

**We need to be EXTREMELY thorough in our search.** Let's examine *every* method of deletion in the system:
1.  `page.destroy`
2.  `leaf.destroy`
3.  `book.destroy`
4.  `DELETE /books/:book_id/pages/:id` (`PagesController#destroy` / `LeafablesController#destroy`)
5.  `Leaf::Editable` (which includes edits, revisions, trash, and the `dup_leafable_with_attachments` methods)
6.  `ActionText::HasMarkdown` and its associated `with_markdown_#{name}_and_embeds` methods

**This demands a *very* comprehensive code search and careful analysis to prevent overlooking any place where orphaned files or records could occur.** It's crucial to identify *all* deletion paths and ensure the necessary cleanup processes for orphaned images are in place. We cannot leave *any* stone unturned!

**Deep Dive into Image Deletion in Writebook**

Okay, so I've been staring at this grep output, and it's screaming at me. There are several key areas where we need to look closer. We have the standard `has_many_attached :uploads` in `ActionText::Markdown`, and then we have the `delegated_type` relationships involving `Leaf` and `Edit`. That's where it's going to get interesting. Specifically, it appears the issue is when we `destroy` a `leaf`.

My immediate concern stems from the `Leaf::Editable` module and the `has_many :edits, dependent: :delete_all` relationship. When a leaf is edited, a new leafable (`Page`) is created with a *new* markdown body, but the old, with the images, persists. The current implementation copies the attachments (images) from the old `Page` to the new one, but because of how `dup_leafable_with_attachments` is implemented, the old `Page` still holds the reference to the `uploads`. Then, when a leaf is destroyed, and edits are *deleted* via SQL, it leaves the orphaned old `Page` with its `markdown_body`, and the attached images. This behavior clearly violates the spec. The spec says that after a page is destroyed and background jobs are complete, neither the image file nor its database record should exist.

It appears the UI calls `@leaf.trashed!`, a soft delete, which records a trash edit, keeping the old `Page`. The actual destruction, which *does* destroy the `Page`, is called when you clear out the stale pages. I need to understand exactly what happens in these different scenarios:

1.  What happens during a `page.destroy`? (which is what we *need* to fix.)
2.  What happens during `leaf.destroy` (various states: never edited, with revisions, trashed)?
3.  What happens during `book.destroy`?
4.  What happens during the `DELETE` request to `leafable_path(leaf)`? Does that soft delete or fully destroy the leafable?

I need to read through the test suite *carefully*. This is no time to make assumptions. I need to know the controllers and models thoroughly. There could be other places where the same code problem arises. I need a comprehensive understanding of what's happening and where.

**The core problem is orphaned attachments.** And the current setup with `delete_all` likely exacerbates this, leaving orphaned records even if `edit` had `dependent: :destroy`! The fix lies in ensuring we clean up those orphaned images when a page, or the structure containing the page, is fully destroyed. The task isn't about *breaking* the existing upload functionality, but ensuring all associated files are removed.

**Deep Dive into Image Upload Lifecycle and Destruction**

Okay, let's break this down. My goal is to ensure that when a page with embedded images is destroyed, *everything* associated with those images is gone – the file, the database record, the whole shebang. No more lingering digital ghosts. And all of this has to work with my current image upload and retrieval processes, which are described above.

My initial thought is to trace the complete lifecycle of image uploads in the app, from the user interface down to the database and storage. I need to understand exactly what happens at each stage:
1.  **Form Rendering:** A markdown editor is part of the Page's edit form. The editor uses `house-md`, which, I now know, integrates with ActiveStorage.
2.  **Upload:** When the editor drops an image, `house-md` sends a `POST` request to `/uploads.json`. This triggers a controller (`UploadsController#create`) that does the critical work of:
    *   Locating the page (`@record`) based on a signed global ID.
    *   Attaching the uploaded file to the page's markdown body (`@markdown.uploads.attach`).
    *   Setting a slug for the `ActiveStorage::Attachment` using `ActiveStorage::Sluggable`.
    *   Returning a JSON response with the image's URL (`@upload.slug_path`).
3.  **Image Retrieval:** Retrieving the image involves another controller (`UploadsController#show`) that:
    *   Finds the `ActiveStorage::Attachment` by its slug.
    *   Redirects to a URL that serves the image file.
4.  **Page Destruction:** This is the core problem! When the page is deleted, I need to ensure that the image file and associated database records (specifically, `ActiveStorage::Blob` records) are also removed.

My analysis reveals that the problem lies in how the `ActiveStorage::Attachment` records are managed during page destruction and subsequent cleanup of the blobs. With `dependent: :destroy` on `has_many_attached :uploads`, the file will not be automatically purged and is stuck on disk. I need to confirm this is happening. The solution involves changing the dependency to `dependent: :purge_later`, which enqueues a background job (`ActiveStorage::PurgeJob`) to handle the file deletion. Once that purge is run, everything will be cleared.

**Deep Dive into Asset Destruction Scenarios**

Okay, here's what I've been thinking through regarding asset management, particularly focusing on how image uploads within ActionText interact with record destruction in this Rails application. The core issue is ensuring that when a page, edit, or associated record is removed, the linked assets (images) are *also* removed. I've broken down several scenarios and what I've found has me very concerned.

Initially, I looked at the initialization order of ActiveStorage relative to my custom extensions. My initial thought was that including `ActiveStorage::Attached::Model` directly within the `ActionText::Markdown` model would be the cleanest approach, bypassing the need for an `ActiveSupport.on_load` block. This seems sound because the engine initializers run first, ensuring the ActiveStorage concerns are in place before other application code tries to use them. I was happy, until I looked closer at edit flow.

First, I traced the cleanest scenario: a direct `page.destroy`. When a page containing an image upload is destroyed, the cascade *should* purge the associated blobs. This chain starts with the `has_markdown :body` association, which then destroys the `ActionText::Markdown` record. Since `ActionText::Markdown` has `has_many_attached :uploads, dependent: :purge_later`, the associated attachments are destroyed, and their blobs are purged *after* the transaction commits. The `dependent: :purge_later` on the attachment is crucial here. I verified the job enqueueing and blob purging behavior, and this scenario appears to work as expected.

However, the real problems begin with scenario 2: Editing a page *after* an image has been uploaded, and then destroying the page. This is where things get messy and where I have found significant problems.

Here's the scenario: an editor uploads an image to a page. They then edit and save the page (causing a new edit to be created and the old one to be saved as an edit). The code *dups* the current leafable (in this case, the `Page`) and applies the changes to the *new* leafable, while saving the old leafable to the edits! The new leafable does *not* have any attachments cloned.  Since `Leaf::Editable` uses `.dup` and then updates, it's essentially creating a *new* `Page` record when there's an edit, *not* updating the original one. The `ActiveStorage::Attachment` remains attached to the *old* page record! The new page has zero uploads. The old one is orphaned.

If the new page (the active page) is destroyed, the old page and its associated attachments are untouched.

If the *leaf* (the link to the page) is destroyed, it *deletes* the edits, but crucially, this `delete_all` skips calling the `destroy` method on the `Edit` objects. The `Edit` *then* points to the *orphaned* `Page` that still contains the `ActiveStorage::Attachment` records and blobs, which are never purged, and the files remain.

I need to confirm these findings through actual testing in a `rails runner` session, but the potential for orphaned assets and data corruption is incredibly concerning. There are multiple scenarios here where assets can be orphaned.

This is a serious problem.

**Deep Dive into the Flaws and Potential Fixes**

Alright, let's take a beat and dissect this. We've got a critical issue here, a real gotcha in the ActiveStorage integration within this Markdown setup. First, let's nail down what we've discovered.

**The Crucial Flaw: `dependent: :destroy` is a Trap**

The heart of the problem lies in that `lib/rails_ext/action_text_markdown.rb` file. Specifically, that line: `has_many_attached :uploads, dependent: :destroy`. The problem is that, with ActiveStorage, `has_many_attached` doesn't behave like a standard ActiveRecord `has_many`. ActiveStorage’s implementation *only* checks for `dependent: :purge_later`. It *ignores* `:destroy`. We can see it in action in other parts of the application: `app/models/book.rb`, `app/models/picture.rb`, `ActionText::RichText` in Rails, and `ActiveStorage::Attachment`'s `purge_dependent_blob_later` method, that explicitly checks for `:purge_later`. The original developer *clearly* assumed the ActiveRecord behavior, and as a result, images are *never* purged after the Markdown record is destroyed. The cascade goes like this: page destroy, markdown destroy, attachment destroy, but, critically, *no* `blob.purge_later`, so files are left stranded on disk. This is a potential data leak, and a storage cost burden, since orphaned files accumulate.

**The Autoloading Gotcha and the Copy-Paste Effect**

The second area of concern is that `ActiveSupport.on_load :active_storage_attachment` block. This line, in `lib/rails_ext/action_text_markdown.rb`, indicates that the original developer didn’t fully grasp the Rails autoloading mechanism. This code is copied from `active_storage_sluggable.rb`, where it's correctly used because `ActiveStorage::Attachment` is loaded lazily. In our case, `ActionText::Markdown` is defined *immediately* above the `on_load` block, meaning it could potentially fail if `active_storage_attachment` wasn’t yet loaded. This is not critical, because of the code change, but is a code smell.

I'm starting to think about this a bit more. I wonder about this flow in the Writebook UI. It makes me want to examine the controller flow when an editor adds an image into a page’s markdown and saves it. And then, most critically, when that page, or leaf, or book is destroyed. I need to understand that entire flow, from the moment an editor clicks "save" to the point where the image should be purged.

**The Path Forward**

So, the fix is straightforward: change that line to `has_many_attached :uploads, dependent: :purge_later`. And then test thoroughly. But...

I'm also curious. If we include `Uploads` directly in `ActionText::Markdown`, or change the option, then is `ActiveStorage::Sluggable` still applied? It should, because `uploads.attach` calls into `ActiveStorage::Attachment` which, because of autoloading, will ensure the `Sluggable` is included immediately. Good. This is better. We need the `dependent: :purge_later` *and* we need to ensure the `Uploads` module is always included, no matter how the app is initialized.

**Next Steps: Let's Trace the UI Interaction**

Now, I want to trace the Writebook UI's behavior. Let's look at `app/views/books/show.html.erb`, `app/views/leaves/_sidebar.html.erb` or the system tests like `test/system/edit_page_test.rb`. We need to trace the user actions through the controller flow to confirm that after the fix, image uploads are correctly purged.

messages.thinking:
**Deep Dive into Image Persistence in Writebook**

Alright, let's break this down systematically. I'm seeing a critical flaw in how Writebook handles embedded images in markdown, specifically in the context of page edits, revisions, and deletions. This is a potential disaster for storage costs and data integrity. Let's dig in.

The initial fix, modifying `ActionText::Markdown` to use `purge_later` instead of `destroy` for attachments, *does* solve the straightforward case of a direct page destruction. If I just call `.destroy` on a page, the attachments, blobs, and files on disk are cleaned up, as expected, once the background job runs. That's a good start, but clearly, it is not enough.

Now, the real issue, the full editor workflow, here's where it all falls apart. Specifically when someone edits a page:

The workflow: an image upload occurs, saving an image to a page's markdown body. The *problem*: when someone saves an *edit*, Writebook's `Leaf::Editable` mechanism *duplicates* the leafable (the page), creates a *new* leafable with the new content, and the old version of the leafable is stashed in the edits.

Here's the problem: The *original* page, with the image attachment, goes into the `edits` history, and the *new* page, that gets displayed to the user, doesn't have any images attached to it. The new page is effectively the first version with the updated text. The image's attachment is sitting on the historical version, and it is *never* purged!

When the page is trashed or destroyed, we destroy the *current* page. The previous page, with the uploaded image's `ActiveStorage::Attachment` and `ActiveStorage::Blob` never get deleted, since the current page doesn't have an attachment pointing to the image. `Leaf::Editable`'s `dependent: :delete_all` on `edits` only *deletes* the edit records, it doesn't actually trigger any purging of the attachments.

Also, `Leaf::Editable`'s `dup_leafable_with_attachments` is only copying the blobs and *not* updating the markdown content with the newly created file URL. Meaning, there is not even a *reference* to this image on the current revision. This breaks the expected behavior.

So what's happening? There are two layers here, `Leaf` and the *Page* itself. Trashing a `Leaf` deletes the page but does not automatically take care of the associated `ActiveStorage::Attachment` and `ActiveStorage::Blob` and the image on disk.

Now, if we were to delete a *book*, that would cascade down through `Leaves` and `Pages`, but still would not purge the images referenced by any historical `Edit`.

The `dup_leafable_with_attachments` method, while well-intentioned, is causing the orphaned attachments. It needs to be carefully examined as to *when* it is appropriate to duplicate attachments, and how we handle purging. We are potentially losing image data from disk and it is staying in the database.

Therefore, the fix, in my considered view, is not a simple tweak to `dependent: :purge_later`, and also not a matter of whether a user can *see* an image -- this is about the underlying data. We need to implement a mechanism that *purges* the previous version's image attachments when an edit occurs, or when the leaf is trashed or the book is destroyed. We need to *explicitly* handle the lifecycle of attachments during editing, revisions, and deletion to ensure they are properly managed. This requires a deeper understanding of the relationships between `Leaf`, `Page`, `Edit`, `ActiveStorage::Attachment`, and `ActiveStorage::Blob` in the Writebook architecture, and potentially altering the way we perform `dup_leafable_with_attachments`.

**Analyzing the Writebook Image Upload Issue**

Okay, here's the situation as I understand it. We've got a problem with image uploads in Writebook, specifically when those images are embedded in markdown. The core issue is that when a page with an embedded image is destroyed, the image file and its tracking records (ActiveStorage::Blob and ActiveStorage::Attachment) aren't being completely removed. They're lingering in the database and storage, leading to increased costs. The goal is to ensure these resources are fully purged when a page is "destroyed," which I've determined means a full ActiveRecord destruction (`page.destroy`, `leaf.destroy`, or `book.destroy`) and not a soft-delete (like trashing). We must find a solution while ensuring existing functionality – namely image uploads and URL retrieval – continues to work as expected.

My investigation begins with the ActiveStorage code. Specifically, the relationship between `ActiveStorage::Blob` and `ActiveStorage::Attachment` needs close examination. I'm focusing on why attachments persist even after the associated markdown record is gone. I've found a crucial detail: the `slug` on the `ActiveStorage::Attachment` is unique. This means that a single image uploaded to a page can only have one corresponding attachment record, which uses that slug to point to the file and `ActiveStorage::Blob`. This becomes important because Writebook uses multiple versions of a `Page` which are all linked to the same file.

I've traced the flow of image uploads through the `UploadsController`, the `ActionText::Markdown` module, and the `Leaf::Editable` concern. I've noted that `Leaf::Editable` creates new `Page` records when a page is edited. Critically, the `uploads` association (the `ActiveStorage::Attachment`) is currently attached to the "old" `Page` when an image is uploaded and attached by `POST /uploads`, rather than the new `Page` created upon save or autosave by `PUT /books/:book_id/pages/:id` with `leaf.edit`. This means that when the live, "new" page is destroyed, any attachments are *not* destroyed. This is the root cause. This also means when history is viewed, even if the "new" page is destroyed, that the image displays because of the unique slug and singular attachment.

My investigation also considers different scenarios to understand the edge cases when the pages are destroyed or purged:

*   **Scenario 1:** Model Level (`page.destroy`)
    *   This includes simply destroying the `Page` object directly.
*   **Scenario 2:** Controller / Integration Level (Upload via `POST /uploads` without `PUT leafable_path`, then `page.destroy`)
    *   I've checked how uploading a file with a `POST /uploads` call, and then immediately deleting the page works.
*   **Scenario 3:** Controller / Integration / System Level (Upload via `POST /uploads`, then `PUT leafable_path(leaf)` to save, then destroy)
    *   I've determined there are **three subcases**, which are important to understand:
        *   **Subcase 3a:** `leaf.reload.page.destroy!`
        *   **Subcase 3b:** `leaf.reload.destroy!`
        *   **Subcase 3c:** `books(:handbook).destroy!`
    *   I've determined that subcase 3a-c all fail to delete the attachments and files completely.

A key revelation is that the `dependent: :destroy` on the `uploads` association in `ActionText::Markdown` is problematic. Destroying `ActionText::Markdown` also destroys `ActiveStorage::Attachment`. This is where the cleanup chain breaks down because the `Blob` isn't purged as expected, even with background jobs, due to the presence of orphaned `Attachment` records. I've seen that `ActiveStorage::Blob` uses the `ActiveRecord::InvalidForeignKey` exception to rescue its own destruction.

To solve this, I'm analyzing the relationships between `Edit`, `Leaf`, and `Leafable` to understand the data flow, and the exact meaning of `dependent: :delete_all` versus `dependent: :destroy` on `has_many :edits`. I am investigating a potential solution where the attachment is transferred to the current page.

I am checking how to modify `Leaf::Editable` and/or the `UploadsController` to make sure the attachment is always tied to the current version of the page being edited.

  class_methods do

      define_method :other_positioned_siblings do

    end

    other_positioned_siblings.before(self).last
  end

  def next
    other_positioned_siblings.after(self).first
  end

      all_to_move = [ self, *followed_by ]
      before, after = before_and_after_for(offset: offset, moving: all_to_move)

2.  **Edit/Revision Attachment Transfer:** We need to handle attachments carefully during page edits (`leaf.edit`). When a page is edited, a new page (`new_leafable`) is created, and the old page moves into edits. The existing logic wasn't transferring embedded images to the new page. The solution? Move `uploads_attachments` to `new_leafable`. Additionally, the previous `leafable`s should be destroyed on `leaf.destroy` so that they do not exist anymore.

3.  **Controller Record Resolution:** The upload controller needs to resolve the correct page record (`record`) to ensure uploads are attached to the current page after a revision, even if stale `record_gid`s are present in the browser. Using `Edit.find_by(leafable: record)&.leaf&.leafable || record` resolves this issue.

Tests that include an attachment to a page directly need to be updated as a result of the fixes proposed.

module Leaf::Editable
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

  MINIMUM_TIME_BETWEEN_VERSIONS = 10.minutes

  included do
    before_destroy :destroy_edited_leafables
    has_many :edits, dependent: :delete_all

    after_update :record_moved_to_trash, if: :was_trashed?
  end

  def edit(leafable_params: {}, leaf_params: {})
    if record_new_edit?(leafable_params)
      update_and_record_edit leaf_params, leafable_params
    else
      update_without_recording_edit leaf_params, leafable_params
    end
  end

  private
    def record_new_edit?(leafable_params)
      will_change_leafable?(leafable_params) && last_edit_old?
    end

    def last_edit_old?
      edits.empty? || edits.last.created_at.before?(MINIMUM_TIME_BETWEEN_VERSIONS.ago)
    end

    def will_change_leafable?(leafable_params)
      leafable_params.select do |key, value|
        leafable.attributes[key.to_s] != value
      end.present?
    end

    def update_without_recording_edit(leaf_params, leafable_params)
      transaction do
        leafable.update!(leafable_params)

        edits.last&.touch
        update! leaf_params
      end
    end

    def update_and_record_edit(leaf_params, leafable_params)
      transaction do
        new_leafable = dup_leafable_with_attachments leafable
        new_leafable.update!(leafable_params)
        transfer_markdown_uploads leafable, new_leafable

        edits.revision.create!(leafable: leafable)
        update! leaf_params.merge(leafable: new_leafable)
      end
    end

    def dup_leafable_with_attachments(leafable)
      leafable.dup.tap do |new|
        leafable.attachment_reflections.each do |name, _|
          new.send(name).attach(leafable.send(name).blob)
        end
      end
    end

    def transfer_markdown_uploads(old_leafable, new_leafable)
      if old_leafable.respond_to?(:markdown_body) && old_leafable.markdown_body&.uploads_attachments&.any?
        new_markdown = new_leafable.body
        new_markdown.save! unless new_markdown.persisted?

        old_leafable.markdown_body.uploads_attachments.update_all(record_id: new_markdown.id)
        old_leafable.markdown_body.uploads.reset
        old_leafable.markdown_body.uploads_attachments.reset
        new_markdown.uploads.reset
        new_markdown.uploads_attachments.reset
      end
    end

    def destroy_edited_leafables
      edits.includes(:leafable).each do |edit|
        edit.leafable.destroy if edit.leafable && edit.leafable != leafable
      end
    end

    def record_moved_to_trash
      edits.trash.create!(leafable: leafable)
    end

    def was_trashed?
      trashed? && previous_changes.include?(:status)
    end
end

**The Root of the `ActiveSupport.on_load` Mystery and the Incorrect Hook Name!**

Aha! I've finally traced the cause of this issue with `ActiveSupport.on_load` and, specifically, the incorrect hook name! The backtrace gave it away: an `undefined method 'has_many_attached'` error on `ActionText::Markdown`. The culprit is the initialization order: application initializers, like the one in `config/initializers/extensions.rb`, run *before* the Rails engine initializers, like the `"active_storage.attached"` initializer within `ActiveStorage::Engine`. Since `Rails::Application` inherits from `Rails::Engine`, its `load_config_initializers` method runs first.

Here's the sequence: `config/initializers/extensions.rb` runs. I'm going to look at the exact differences, hunk by hunk, comparing the working directory with the index or HEAD, as appropriate. I want to scrutinize every single modification, every added line, every removed line. Are there any formatting issues? Any unexpected code changes I made without realizing? messages.content:
I have resolved the issue so that destroying a page whose markdown embeds uploaded images completely removes both the database records tracking those images and their underlying files once background purge jobs finish running, while preserving the existing markdown image upload and retrieval flow:

1. **Purge markdown upload blobs on destruction & ensure association availability (`lib/rails_ext/action_text_markdown.rb`, `lib/rails_ext/action_text_has_markdown.rb`)**:
   - Changed `has_many_attached :uploads, dependent: :destroy` to `has_many_attached :uploads, dependent: :purge_later` (`ActiveStorage::Attachment` only enqueues `ActiveStorage::PurgeJob` when `dependent == :purge_later`; `:destroy` caused the `ActiveStorage::Blob` record and its file on disk to never be purged).
   - Included `ActionText::Markdown::Uploads` during `config.to_prepare` instead of waiting on `ActiveSupport.on_load :active_storage_attachment`, ensuring `uploads` and its `dependent: :destroy` attachment association are always registered even before `ActiveStorage::Attachment` is autoloaded.
   - Updated `with_markdown_#{name}_and_embeds` to preload `uploads_attachments: :blob`.

2. **Keep markdown uploads associated with the active page across edits & clean up revisions (`app/models/leaf/editable.rb`, `app/models/leaf.rb`, `app/models/leaf/searchable.rb`, `app/controllers/action_text/markdown/uploads_controller.rb`)**:
